payload.purpose_context: Data-protection terms require a current, change-notified list of sub-processors. Today that list is prose that nothing checks or publishes. This mission adds an optional catalog file with validation, a machine-readable export, a change feed, a generated list page and a link to the measures catalog. The toolkit supplies the structure; each site supplies its own facts. Tracks issue #403 in epic #400.
payload.purpose_tldr: Let a documentation site keep a validated list of its sub-processors and announce changes to it.

options: Split into a later WP gated on #359 (recommended)
payload.question: Issue #359 (generated-section contract) is still open. How should this mission handle the generated sub-processor list page? (1) Split it into a final WP that waits on #359 being accepted, while the catalog, validation, agent API, change feed, tom_classification link and docs ship independently. (2) Build it now following #359's drafted contract (generated: {by, at, source_digest} stamp plus a --check drift gate), clearly marked provisional in ADR-0085 and on the page.

payload.final_answer: Split into a later WP gated on #359 (recommended). Decider: operator (answered 'go', relayed by dispatcher 2026-11-23). Final WP builds on ADR-0087 (PR #445; Proposed on GitHub at time of recording) once it is accepted and merged.

options: A: dedicated RSS + JSON changes from since/until (recommended)
payload.question: With the generated page deferred, what is the sub-processor change feed? (A) A dedicated RSS feed (subprocessors.xml), one item per addition (since) and per removal (until), plus the same entries as a changes list in api/subprocessors.json. Derived only from since/until, and carrying dates rather than a build-time 'current/upcoming' status so builds stay byte-stable. A future-dated since or until is how a site gives advance notice. (B) The same, but entries come from changelog fragments instead of since/until. (C) Only the JSON changes list in the agent API, with no RSS feed until the page WP.

payload.final_answer: A: dedicated RSS feed subprocessors.xml (one item per since=added, per until=removed) plus the same entries as 'changes' in api/subprocessors.json; derived only from since/until; dates only, no build-time status (byte-stable); a future-dated since/until is the advance-notice mechanism. Decider: operator ('2A', relayed verbatim by dispatcher 2026-11-23).

options: A: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 list + optional location_note (recommended)
C: free text now, structured later
payload.question: Record field set (⚖ counsel reviews it before it is called DPA-ready). Fields as in the issue: { id, name, address?, contact?, processing, location, responsibilities, since, until?, external_references?, tom_classification? }. external_references reuses the existing page shape (inline or {type: biblio, id}), and tom_classification reuses the page field shape from ADR-0080. Open point: how is  typed? (A) A non-empty list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes (e.g. [DE, US]) with an optional free-text location_note. Machine-checkable, useful later for transfer analysis. (B) Free text. (C) Free text now, structured later. No transfer-mechanism field in any case; that is a follow-up issue.

payload.final_answer: A: location is a non-empty list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes plus an optional free-text location_note; transfer-mechanism field out of scope (follow-up issue). (Question text lost the word 'location' to a shell-quoting slip; the question was how 'location' is typed.) Decider: operator ('1A', relayed verbatim by dispatcher 2026-11-23, mapped by dispatcher to option A of this DM).

options: A: fail at config setup in a file-gated integration (recommended)
B: fail when the route renders
payload.question: Where does an invalid sub-processor catalog fail the build? (A) In a new doc-kitty:subprocessors integration at astro:config:setup. It reads the file once, validates it with the shared bare-Node core (the same core validate-catalog.mjs imports) against the bibliography and measures catalogs, and throws one aggregate error before any page renders. It injects /api/subprocessors.json and /subprocessors.xml only when the file exists (gherkin precedent), so served-surface detection drives the api/index.json links. (B) Lazily, when the routes render. Simpler, but the error comes late and a missing route cannot be told apart from a failed one.

payload.final_answer: A: fail at astro:config:setup in a new file-gated doc-kitty:subprocessors integration; validate once with the shared bare-Node core; one aggregate error before rendering; routes injected only when the file exists. Engineering alignment confirmed as written (pure core + bare-Node loader, bibliography/measures ids passed in, embedded ISO alpha-2 list, RSS reuses rss.ts helpers, WP01-WP05 with WP05 gated on #445). Decider: operator ('as recommended', relayed verbatim by dispatcher 2026-11-23).
